label: Identify Heart Sounds
description: Listen to each sound and decide whether it matches the question.

questions.prompt: Is this a normal heart sound?
questions.explanation: Only S1 and S2 are present. S1 is closure of the mitral and tricuspid valves, S2 is closure of the aortic and pulmonic valves.

questions.prompt: Is this a normal heart sound?
questions.explanation: There is a harsh crescendo-decrescendo murmur between S1 and S2. This is aortic stenosis.
The extra sound comes in early diastole, just after S2, with a 'Ken-tuck-y' cadence.
The extra sound comes in late diastole, just before S1, with a 'Ten-nes-see' cadence. This is an S4 gallop.
The extra sound comes just before S1, from the atria contracting into a stiff ventricle.
A sharp, high-pitched sound falls between S1 and S2. It is typical of mitral valve prolapse.
The murmur stays at the same loudness from S1 to S2 (holosystolic). This is mitral regurgitation, not the diamond-shaped murmur of aortic stenosis.
